title: Graceful degradation hint protocol with latency fencing and soft-circuiting
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Summary: Implement a graceful degradation 'hint protocol' that combines latency-based fencing, geo pinning hints, and capacity-aware soft-circuiting to reduce cross-region tail latency while preserving customer traffic locality and minimizing failed requests during regional overloads. This ticket covers the design, prototype, and staged rollout of the protocol in the global request director service.

Goals:
- Reduce p95/p99 cross-region tail latency by preferring local/nearby regions when they meet latency SLOs, but transparently failover to warm fallback regions when capacity is constrained.
- Avoid hard ejects that cause wholesale switchover; introduce soft-circuiting (request-level shed) and a hint propagation mechanism so downstream services can make informed cache/batch decisions.
- Provide observability: per-route SLO health, capacity headroom, hint hit/miss rates, and shed counts.
- Ensure incremental rollout: start with read-only model endpoints and low-traffic routes, exercise chaos testing, then expand to high-traffic generation endpoints.

Design overview:
- Latency fencing: each region advertises a rolling latency quantile profile (p50/p90/p99) for model endpoints per-configured sequence-length buckets. Router computes a region score = latency_penalty + capacity_penalty + affinity_bonus. Regions with score below a fence threshold are eligible primary targets.
- Geo pinning with soft override: maintain customer->region affinity (pin) for session tokens. Allow override when pinned region is ineligible for the incoming request (score above fence) and alternate is within regulated fallback list. The router emits a pin_hint header: {pin_region, chosen_region, reason_code}.
- Capacity-aware steering: regions report realtime headroom (tokens/sec or inflight-requests) and a probabilistic soft-shed probability is computed to shed low-priority or large-context requests before escalation. Shedding decisions are signaled in the hint header and logged for SLO analysis.
- Circuit breaker layers: short-window fast breakers (per-host) and longer-window capacity circuits (per-region model pool). Fast breakers return 429-like soft responses and set a short cache TTL; capacity circuits trigger gradual rerouting with exponential backoff to the pinned region.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We favor soft, probabilistic shedding over aggressive global ejection to preserve availability and avoid cascading failovers. This accepts a slight increase in 429s for large/batch requests in exchange for reduced p99 latency spikes.
- Hint propagation increases header size and complexity; we limit hints to a compact token and a reason code to keep overhead low.
- Accurate headroom signals require tighter telemetry windows; we will use a 5s streaming window for headroom with smoothing to avoid oscillation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router returns pin_hint headers on at least 95% of routed requests in canary region.
- p99 latency for cross-region routed requests reduces by at least 20% in canary traffic compared to baseline over a 24h window.
- No more than 2% increase in global error rate attributable to the new soft-shed behavior during canary.
- Dashboards surface hint hit rate, shed rate, region score distributions, and SLO delta.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in staging: implement scoring and hint emission; validate with synthetic traffic (Marina + Alex).
2) Canary in a single non-critical region (us-west-2 for internal test orgs) for read-only embedding endpoints (1 week).
3) Expand to generator endpoints with low traffic percentage (5%) and monitor.
4) If stable, enable for broader traffic with throttled rollout and automatic rollback on threshold breaches.

Monitoring & Metrics:
- Emit metrics: routing.chosen_region, routing.pin_region, routing.reason_code, routing.score_components (latency, capacity, affinity), routing.soft_shed=true/false.
- Alerts: routing.soft_shed_rate > 1% for more than 10m on production routes -> investigate autoscaler and capacity.
- SLOs to track: route_p95_latency, route_p99_latency, route_error_rate.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic latency/capacity vectors.
- Integration tests: hint header correctness, fallback behavior, and re-routing under simulated overloads.
- Chaos tests: network partition (simulate region outage) and abrupt capacity drop to verify graceful reroute and no double-counting of inflight requests.

Open decisions:
- Exact fence threshold tuning and whether it should be per-customer tier. Proposal: start with global threshold and evaluate per-tier tuning in follow-up ticket.
- Which request attributes should increase shedding priority (long context, high temperature, batch size).

Implementation notes:
- Router change in service: request-director v2 with scoring module. PR will add a small proto for hint header and a runtime-config flag to enable canary toggles.
- Downstream: runtime runtime-plugins must read pin_hint to prewarm KV cache and adapt batching sizes. Work with infra/plugins team to add prewarm hooks.

Security & Compliance:
- Hints contain no PII; only region codes and reason codes. Ensure header is not logged verbatim in user-accessible logs.

comments: 2025-02-21 - Ethan: Initial spike completed. Implemented scoring prototype in a sandbox router. Observed oscillation when headroom sampling was <2s; moving to 5s smoothing window.
2025-02-25 - Marina: Design review with SREs. Agreed to limit hint header size and keep reason codes compact. SRE requested a kill-switch toggle at the director-level for immediate rollback.

2025-02-28 - PR feedback (Alex): Added unit tests for scoring edge cases. Flagged a potential race where pin_hint could cause downstream KV warmers to prewarm the wrong model version; added version_tag to hint payload as mitigation.

2025-03-02 - Load test (loadeng-team): 12h synthetic run with 30% cross-region traffic. p99 reduced by ~23% for targeted routes; soft-shed rate averaged 0.9%. Logging indicates most sheds were long-context (>8k tokens) requests.
2025-03-04 - Marina: Canary toggle prepared. Plan to enable on staging and then 1% production for embeddings this week. Noting follow-up tickets for per-tier thresholds and runtime plugin updates.
